Subject: Re: Pilot pricing clarification — quantized models

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and the ML team reviewed the basic terms and we have a few open questions before we can move the PoC forward:

- Our engineering team wants to confirm whether Redwood’s pricing differentiates between full-precision and quantized model variants (e.g., int8/4-bit). If so, can you provide the unit cost delta and any performance caveats?
- We're planning a 6-week timeboxed evaluation (3 environments: sandbox, staging, light-prod). We'd like an example packaging proposal that maps to our expected token burn (attached is an estimated scope).
- Procurement would like to see a non-binding MOU that lays out pricing bands and a conditional SLA uplift for production conversion (if we hit agreed throughput).

I attached the Cipher PoC scope document for context (Cipher_PoC_Scope.docx). Can you send a short pricing matrix and a suggested mutual action plan by EOD Friday?

Best,
Emma Lowe
Procurement Lead | Cipher Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot pricing clarification — quantized models

Hi Emma —

Appreciate the clear scope — that's helpful. Quick answers up front and then an attached matrix with three compact options.

Summary answers:
1) Quantized variants: Yes — we publish a discounted rate for quantized model variants that reflects lower GPU memory and improved throughput on our runtime. Typical list deltas are 20–35% off the standard token rate depending on architecture and quantization level. The attached sheet (PoC_Pricing_Options_v2.xlsx) shows model-level examples (GPT-like-7B / Quantized-8bit = -25%). There are trade-offs on edge-case sampling quality; we can map those to your eval prompts.

2) Packaging: I included three proposals in the sheet — Timebox (fixed price for 6 weeks with capped token burn), Flexible bucket (prepaid tokens + overage), and Hybrid seat+token (small baseline seat fee + tokens). Each row shows estimated cost for the token burn profile you sent.

3) MOU / SLA uplift: We can provide a non-binding MOU and conditional SLA uplift tied to a short production readiness checklist. For example, if you commit to a 3-month minimum at conversion with the 20% commit tier, we provide a 99.9% P95 latency SLA and a dedicated escalation channel. Draft MOU template linked below; we'll convert to DocuSign once we have alignment.

Next steps I recommend:
- Quick 30-minute alignment call to review the spreadsheet and confirm the quantization candidates (Tue/Wed next week).
- We prepare a one-page MOU and a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones (ingest test, latency gate, final decision).

Attachments: PoC_Pricing_Options_v2.xlsx, SLA_Table.pdf

Can you confirm Tue/Wed availability? Karthik — can you join the MAP call and own commercial mapping? Marissa — looping you for manager-level signoff thresholds if we need to offer a one-time accelerator discount (not standard list).

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
